correctness.rationale: The stationary bivariate OU Lyapunov solution and pair Gaussian covariance were reconstructed. Orthogonal sum/difference conditioning gives a positive-definite two-by-two Schur complement and exact Gaussian KL. The noiseless rational expression was evaluated and checked by an independent direct four-by-four Gaussian inverse. Expanding it yields sigma and first-order finite-sampling loss; the noisy exact expression is analytic after h=zt substitution, giving sensor loss h/t. Strict path-to-endpoint KL contraction uses non-endpoint-measurable signed area, localizing all maximizers; equicoercivity then yields t_h/sqrt(h/kappa)->1 and max J_h/sigma=1-2sqrt(kappa h)+o(sqrt h). The delivered standard-library checker passed 64 deterministic checks. The result does not assert finite-h uniqueness.

value.rationale: The theorem answers a natural mathematical measurement-design problem for the same Brownian engine already studied at finite time resolution: independent detector noise suppresses the small-lag time arrow whereas coarse time resolution loses path information. A sharp universal optimum sqrt(h/kappa), for all possible global optimizers, and an exact leading relative distinguishability loss 2sqrt(kappa h) quantify the competing scales. It is neither a numerical parameter substitution nor merely the previously known continuous entropy-production rate. It is limited to pairwise KL under matched proportional readout noise, not an assertion about finite-sample inferential power.
